findings.title: Workflow reminder cancellations are not awaited when cancelling bookings
findings.body: In handleCancelBooking, deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called inside forEach loops without collecting or awaiting their promises. The handler then continues and returns. In Next.js/serverless execution the process may be frozen after the response, so the database update marking email reminders as cancelled or the SMS cancellation may never complete. This can leave reminders active for cancelled bookings and cause emails/SMS to still be sent.

findings.title: Paid booking cancellation path skips workflow reminder cancellation
findings.body: When bookingToDelete.paid is true, handleCancelBooking refunds the payment and returns before reaching the code that cancels scheduled jobs and workflow reminders. As a result, paid bookings that are rejected/cancelled do not have their workflow reminders cancelled, so reminder emails or SMS can still be sent for these bookings.

findings.title: Reschedule path uses immediateDelete but leaves old email reminder rows active
findings.body: When rescheduling, old email reminders are cancelled with immediateDelete=true. deleteScheduledEmailReminder's immediate path only calls SendGrid and does not delete the WorkflowReminder row or set cancelled=true. Since the original booking is not deleted, the old reminder row remains scheduled=true and cancelled=false. If the SendGrid cancellation fails or the un-awaited call does not finish, there is no database state to retry or prevent the old reminder from being sent.

findings.title: Cron cancellation query does not restrict to valid scheduled email reminders
findings.body: The remindersToCancel query selects all WorkflowReminder rows with cancelled=true but does not filter by method=EMAIL, scheduled=true, or referenceId non-null. The code then posts reminder.referenceId to SendGrid as batch_id. Any SMS reminder or email reminder with a null referenceId in this state will cause an invalid SendGrid request, which can abort the cancellation loop for all reminders.

findings.title: One failed cancellation aborts processing of all remaining cancelled reminders
findings.body: The SendGrid cancellation loop is wrapped in a single try/catch. If any one client.request or delete fails, execution jumps to the catch block and the remaining cancelled reminders are neither cancelled in SendGrid nor deleted from the database. The endpoint then continues and may return success. A single bad or stale reminder can therefore block cancellation of all cancelled workflow emails on every cron run.

findings.title: Unscheduled reminder query does not exclude cancelled reminders
findings.body: The unscheduledReminders query filters only on method=EMAIL and scheduled=false; it does not exclude rows where cancelled=true. If a reminder ever reaches this state due to a race condition, manual data correction, or future code change, the cron will schedule and send an email for a cancelled booking. The query should exclude cancelled=true rows.

findings.title: immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but does not delete or mark the reminder record
findings.body: deleteScheduledEmailReminder's immediateDelete branch cancels the SendGrid scheduled send but returns without deleting the WorkflowReminder row or setting cancelled=true. Only callers that immediately cascade-delete the reminder can tolerate this, and even there the call is not awaited. For callers such as rescheduling, this leaves stale scheduled reminder rows and removes any ability to retry a failed cancellation.

findings.title: Deferred cancellation can still send imminent reminders
findings.body: For non-immediate cancellations, deleteScheduledEmailReminder only sets cancelled=true, while the cron job cancels SendGrid emails only when the scheduled date is within the next hour and runs every 15 minutes. If a booking is cancelled shortly before a reminder is due, for example a few minutes before sending, the reminder may be sent before the cron job performs the SendGrid cancellation. Near-term reminders should be cancelled synchronously or immediately.

findings.title: requestReschedule does not await reminder cancellation
findings.body: In the requestReschedule mutation, deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called inside a forEach loop without awaiting the promises. The mutation can return before the email reminders are marked cancelled or SMS cancellations complete, so old reminders for a rescheduled booking may still be sent.

findings.title: Workflow deletion cancels external scheduled messages without awaiting them
findings.body: When deleting a workflow, scheduled reminders are cancelled with async deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls inside forEach, and then the workflow is deleted without awaiting those operations. Because deleting the workflow cascades to reminder rows, if the external SendGrid/Twilio cancellation does not finish or fails, no database record remains to retry and the scheduled email/SMS may still be sent.

findings.title: Workflow update mutation does not await async step processing
findings.body: In the workflow update mutation, userWorkflow.steps.map(async ...) performs step deletion/update, reminder cancellation, and reminder creation, but the returned promises are not awaited. The mutation can return before these operations complete, leaving workflow steps, active event types, or reminders in an inconsistent state, especially in serverless environments.

findings.title: Failed SMS cancellation leaves reminder active with no retry
findings.body: deleteScheduledSMSReminder calls twilio.cancelSMS and only deletes the WorkflowReminder if that call succeeds. If the Twilio request throws, the error is swallowed and the reminder row remains scheduled. There is no cancelled state or retry mechanism for SMS reminders, so a transient provider failure can result in an SMS reminder still being sent for a cancelled or rescheduled booking.
